import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.RamseyNumbers
import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1014

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1014](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1014)
- [Er71] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems in graph theory and combinatorial analysis. Combinatorial
  Mathematics and its Applications (Proc. Conf., Oxford, 1969) (1971), 97-109.
- [OpenAI26] *On the ratio of $R(k,\ell)$ and $R(k,\ell+1)$*, proof due to an internal model at
  OpenAI (2026).
  https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/6dc7175d-d9e7-4b8d-96b8-48fe5798cd5b/Ramsey.pdf
-/

open Filter

open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1014

open RamseyNumbers

/--
Let $R(k,l)$ be the Ramsey number, so the minimal $n$ such that every graph on at least $n$
vertices contains either a $K_k$ or an independent set on $l$ vertices.

Prove, for fixed $k\geq 3$, that
$$\lim_{l\to \infty}\frac{R(k,l+1)}{R(k,l)}=1.$$

This has been
[solved](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/6dc7175d-d9e7-4b8d-96b8-48fe5798cd5b/Ramsey.pdf)
by an internal model at OpenAI.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1014.lean"]
theorem erdos_1014 : ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k →
    Tendsto (fun l : ℕ ↦ (R(k, l + 1) : ℝ) / (R(k, l) : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

/--
That proof in fact shows that
$$R(k,l+1)\leq (1+O(l^{-c/k^2}))R(k,l)$$
for some constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1014.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ l : ℕ in atTop,
      (R(k, l + 1) : ℝ) ≤ (1 + C * (l : ℝ) ^ (-c / (k : ℝ) ^ 2)) * (R(k, l) : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1014

reformulations.difference: The imported Ramsey-number definition takes the natural-number infimum of a predicate on graphs with exactly n vertices, expressed by excluding simultaneous clique-freeness of the graph and its complement. The source describes the minimum threshold for all graphs on at least n vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Complement cliques are independent sets, and negating the conjunction of the two clique-free predicates is equivalent to the required clique-or-independent-set alternative. Relabeling handles arbitrary finite vertex sets. Monotonicity in the vertex count gives IsGraphRamsey n k l iff it holds for every m ≥ n. Finite Ramsey's theorem makes the defining set nonempty, so its natural-number infimum is its minimum, not a default zero. These predicate equivalences and nonemptiness were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry.

reformulations.difference: The source's big-O upper bound is expanded into an eventual inequality with an existential real constant C, without explicitly requiring C > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For k ≥ 3 and eventually positive l, R(k,l) > 0 and R(k,l+1) ≥ R(k,l). Consequently the displayed inequality is equivalent to bounding the absolute value of R(k,l+1)/R(k,l) − 1 by C times l^(−c/k²), exactly the standard big-O condition. The power is nonnegative, so any witness C can also be replaced by max C 1. The quantifiers correctly make c independent of k while allowing the bound constant and tail threshold to depend on fixed k. Both the full big-O equivalence and the positive-constant equivalence were proved in the scratch file.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully match the cited sources. The problem page records an affirmative solution verified in Lean, consistent with the metadata. The uniform exponent is also supported by the cited proof: its choice q = k² and estimates in equation (3), after absorbing logarithmic factors for each fixed k, yield an absolute positive multiple of 1/k². Boundary checks proved R(k,0)=0 and R(k,1)=1 for k>0; the exceptional l=0 ratio and inequality do not affect atTop statements. Exhaustive small-graph tests reproduced R(3,0)=0, R(3,1)=1, R(3,2)=3, and R(3,3)=6. The consolidated scratch file compiles, and its equivalence and definition-check lemmas have no sorryAx dependencies. A Nat.find/sInf bridge confirms that the linked proof uses the same Ramsey numbers. The external proof itself was inspected rather than rebuilt under its older Lean 4.29.1 toolchain.
